message.content:
Let the special face \(F\) have probability

\[
p=P(F)>\frac16.
\]

Let the opposite face have probability \(q\). Since the other four faces each have probability \(\frac16\),

\[
p+q+\frac46=1
\]

so

\[
p+q=\frac13.
\]

When two dice are rolled, the sum is \(7\) exactly when the faces are opposite pairs: \((1,6),(2,5),(3,4)\).

One opposite pair is \((F,\text{opposite of }F)\), contributing

\[
2pq.
\]

The other two opposite pairs have probabilities \(\frac16\) and \(\frac16\), so together they contribute

\[
2\left(\frac16\cdot\frac16\right)+2\left(\frac16\cdot\frac16\right)
= \frac{1}{18}+\frac{1}{18}
= \frac19.
\]

Thus

\[
2pq+\frac19=\frac{47}{288}.
\]

So

\[
2pq=\frac{47}{288}-\frac19
=\frac{47}{288}-\frac{32}{288}
=\frac{15}{288}
=\frac{5}{96},
\]

\[
pq=\frac{5}{192}.
\]

Now \(p,q\) have sum \(\frac13\) and product \(\frac{5}{192}\). They are roots of

\[
t^2-\frac13t+\frac{5}{192}=0.
\]

The roots are

\[
\frac{5}{24},\quad \frac18.
\]

Since \(p>\frac16\) and \(q<\frac16\),

\[
p=\frac{5}{24}.
\]

Thus \(m=5\), \(n=24\), and

\[
m+n=29.
\]

The answer is 29.
